correctness.rationale: Coverage by rational tangents dualizes to a blocking set. For a geometrically integral cubic in p>3, its irreducible dual has degree at most six by intersecting with a general dual line and pulling back to a polar conic. It cannot be a line: concurrency of the tangents would make the quadratic directional derivative toward that point vanish identically on the cubic and hence as a polynomial, which in p>3 would make the cubic independent of one variable and geometrically reducible. Thus p+1>6 excludes a full dual line. Blokhuis gives 3(p+1)/2, while distinct smooth points have distinct tangents by Bézout. For p=11,13, Hasse forces exactly 18,21 points respectively. A geometrically integral singular cubic has at most p+2 rational points by its genus-zero normalization and unique possible singular point; a ground-field irreducible geometrically reducible cubic has no smooth rational point because its three lines are Frobenius-conjugate. The published prime-field bound covers p≥17. For the remaining smooth cubics, an origin exists by Hasse, and the short-Weierstrass classification exhausts pointed curves. Any rational degree-three embedding arises from O_E(2O+T), modulo translation by a rational point (hence modulo 3E(F_p)) and projective basis change. For T=(r,s), s≠0, Y=(y+s)/(x−r) has simple poles at T and O and is regular at −T, so 1,x,Y form a basis of L(2O+T); substitution yields the stated cubic. Independent exact finite-field computations confirmed both single scaling orbits; the listed cosets have sizes 6,6,6 and 7,7,7 and exhaust the underlying groups. The six (points, tangents, coverage) triples are (18,18,114), (18,18,112) twice; (21,21,145), (21,21,156) twice, strictly below 133 and 183. The F_7 witness covers all 57 points by twelve tangents, and the gradient argument excludes common nonzero zeros even over the algebraic closure.
residual_risks: The descent/classification and blocking-set bounds are mathematical inputs, not certified by the finite computation. The result does not extend to nonprime fields or to any larger degree on this evidence.
